title: Lean / Python / Colab / Excel Crosswalk Readout v0

canonical_node.axiom: Every claim must be typed, supported, and guarded according to its actual evidence layer; no layer may be inflated beyond what it proves.
definitions: Lane4 Typed Canon: a discipline layer that classifies items into types such as Primitive, Definition, Theorem, BridgePrinciple, etc., and dictates which types may become Lean axioms, definitions, proof targets, or metadata.

Lean proof surface: the set of authored Lean 4 files and theorems, with proof strength categories (definition, wrapper, trivial marker, finite decidable, simplification, substantive case proof, domain judgment, needs source path).
Python/Colab runtime packet: the collection of notebooks and scripts with runtime status (not_declared, open_or_conflicted, claims_verified, mixed_verified_and_open) and evidence classes.

Excel Canonical Ledger: the workbook with sheets for canonical rows, repair summary, staging, alignment, missing rows, false positives, open guards, proof strength, and Python/Colab audit; currently placeholder-heavy.
Open Guards: explicit guardrails that limit claims, such as fixed-point existence is partial, timestamp evidence proves existence not truth, and certain bridges remain open.
derivation: The Excel ledger has 270 rows with placeholder statuses for definition, python, colab, wolfram, empirical, and numerical support; only 56 lean_match_status are SUPPORTED, 171 PARTIAL, 42 NEEDS_SOURCE_PATH, 1 DOMAIN_JUDGMENT_NOT_LEAN_PROOF.

Lane4 Typed Canon provides the strongest discipline layer, with counts of types and a rule that only true primitives become Lean axioms, definitions become definitions, theorems become proof targets, and predictions/protocols/evidence nodes stay outside the proof kernel.

Lean files show no active sorry/admit markers in inspected authored folders, but Proof Strength Summary shows many entries are wrappers (193), declarations (281), definitional (451), finite decidable (58), simplification (189), substantive (43), trivial (352).

Python/Colab packet has 20 notebooks and 5 scripts; status counts: 11 not_declared, 5 open_or_conflicted, 3 claims_verified, 6 mixed; best runtime support is test_master_equation.py with 9 passed tests.

Open Guards list key limitations: fixed-point existence is partial, timestamp evidence proves existence not truth, public evidence pages are review summaries, independent review requires reproducible source, Lagrangian-to-product-form bridge remains conditional, design-to-moral-character step must be defended.
The recommended crosswalk sheet and repair order are specified to join the layers without overclaiming.
canonical_node.action: Create a repaired copy of the Excel ledger named 'Lean 4 - CANONICAL_LEDGER_V2.crosswalk_repair.xlsx', add a 'LEAN_PYTHON_COLAB_EXCEL_CROSSWALK' sheet with the specified columns, and populate it using Lane4 for claim typing, Lean for formal support, Python/Colab for runtime support, and Open Guards for public-status limits. Rewrite public claims to match actual support levels.
boundary: Does not claim that the Excel ledger is fully aligned or ready as a joined proof/evidence ledger.
Does not claim that all Lean theorems are substantive proofs; marker theorems and definitional proofs are labeled as such.
Does not claim that notebook evidence is public-grade until rerun, saved, hashed, and classified.
Does not claim that the Lagrangian-to-product-form bridge or design-to-moral-character derivation is closed.
Does not use raw file counts as evidence; counts must be filtered to exclude build artifacts and internals.
test: Check that every V2 row has a typed_canon_id and claim_type from Lane4.
Check that every Lean support entry has a proof strength classification from the allowed list.
Check that every Python/Colab artifact has a runtime status and evidence class.
Check that every public claim has a public_status value from the allowed list and references an open guard if applicable.
Check that no claim states 'Lean proves the Master Equation' without the qualified wording provided.

dg1_dependencies: Lane4 Typed Canon (typed-canon-reclassification.csv, typed-canon-summary.md, TheophysicsCanon.lean, TheophysicsModules.lean)
Lean proof surface (authored .lean files in EVIDENCE, MASTER_EQUATION, Lane4 folders)
Python/Colab runtime packet (readiness summary, inventory, claim runtime matrix, status register)
Excel Canonical Ledger (CANONICAL_LEDGER_V2.xlsx and Python Colab Audit copy)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a crosswalk that joins claim type, Lean proof strength, Python/Colab runtime status, and open guards into a single ledger, enabling accurate public claim wording and preventing overclaiming.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing discipline of Lane4, the no-sorry Lean core, the cautious Python/Colab packet, and the structural architecture of the Excel ledger.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this crosswalk, the Excel ledger remains placeholder-heavy, public claims risk overstatement, and the layers remain unjoined, leading to potential misrepresentation of evidence strength.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Create crosswalk sheet and repair ledger as specified; do not treat as proof of any underlying claims.

overstatement_risks: Treating the Excel ledger as fully joined when it is placeholder-heavy.
Treating all Lean theorems as substantive proofs without labeling proof strength.
Citing notebook evidence as public-grade without rerun and saved outputs.
Claiming the Lagrangian-to-product-form bridge is closed.
Using raw file counts as evidence without filtering.
kill_conditions: If the crosswalk sheet is not created or populated as specified.
If public claims are rewritten without matching actual support levels.
If open guards are removed or hidden.
If the repaired ledger is presented as proof of theological identifications or closed physics bridges.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the crosswalk as a data structure in Lean, if desired, but the primary target is the Excel ledger repair.

plain_summary: This document audits the current state of Lean proofs, Python/Colab runtime artifacts, and Excel ledgers, concluding that the pieces exist but are not fully joined. It recommends creating a crosswalk sheet to type every claim, attach proof strength, runtime status, and open guards, and rewrite public claims to match actual support. The document itself is a meta-claim about the state of the project, not a proof of any underlying physics or theology.
